title: State and User Interaction
subtitle: Create dynamic interfaces using component state.
description: Learn how state works, how user actions update state and how React automatically re-renders the interface when data changes.

blocks.text: PAGE 1 — Understand State and User Interaction

Welcome to Lesson 4: State and User Interaction. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “State and User Interaction”. The goal is to create dynamic interfaces using component state.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.
State represents information that can change over time and affects what a component displays. Updating state tells React to render the interface again with the new value.

blocks.text: What to notice: focus on the part of the sample that demonstrates Create dynamic interfaces using component state. Identify the input, the operation, and the result before making changes.

blocks.question: A counter is updated by mutating an object already stored in state. What is safer?
options: Directly change its nested value only.
Create a new state value with an immutable update.
Store the value in JSX text only.
Reload the whole browser on each click.
blocks.explanation: React state updates should replace changed arrays/objects rather than mutating them in place.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. React state updates should replace changed arrays/objects rather than mutating them in place.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. React state updates should replace changed arrays/objects rather than mutating them in place.

blocks.question: Two components need to display the same selected course. Where should the shared state usually live?
options: In two independent copies that may disagree.
Only inside CSS.
In the closest common parent that needs to coordinate them.
In a component that does not render either one and is never connected.
blocks.explanation: Lifting state to a common owner avoids conflicting copies of the same fact.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Lifting state to a common owner avoids conflicting copies of the same fact.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Lifting state to a common owner avoids conflicting copies of the same fact.

blocks.text: Do not mutate an existing array or object in state directly. Create a new value using a spread, map, filter, or other immutable update so React can observe the change predictably.

blocks.title: Sample 3: State and User Interaction in practice

blocks.question: A displayed total can be computed from other state values. What is often best?
options: Store a third copy and manually update all three.
Use an effect to rewrite it on every keystroke by default.
Let the values become inconsistent.
Derive the total during render when practical.
blocks.explanation: Derived values reduce duplicated state and synchronization bugs.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Derived values reduce duplicated state and synchronization bugs.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Derived values reduce duplicated state and synchronization bugs.

blocks.text: PAGE 3 — Apply it and check your reasoning
Keep state at the lowest shared component that needs it. Storing the same fact in multiple places creates synchronization bugs; derive values from existing state when practical.

blocks.question: A learner’s XP changes after every correct answer. Which design is easiest to maintain?
options: Repeat the current XP number in many places.
Store XP in one appropriately scoped variable and update it deliberately.
Use a different variable name for every update.
Convert XP to a text label before doing arithmetic.
blocks.explanation: One well-defined source of truth prevents values from drifting apart.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. One well-defined source of truth prevents values from drifting apart.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. One well-defined source of truth prevents values from drifting apart.

blocks.question: A setting must never be reassigned during the program. What should you choose?
options: A constant or immutable binding supported by the language.
A global variable that any function can change.
A string containing the setting name.
A loop that resets the value repeatedly.
blocks.explanation: Constants communicate intent and help prevent accidental reassignment.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Constants communicate intent and help prevent accidental reassignment.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Constants communicate intent and help prevent accidental reassignment.
